extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners, patent applicants and their agents (practitioners before KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards governing KIPO patent examination, decisions to grant or reject, cancellations, reexamination procedures, and requirements for foreign-language applications (including Korean translation rules). Applicable to examiners and applicants/agents preparing or responding to office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of written decision to grant a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The written decision to grant a patent shall include an application number, title of invention, name and address of applicant and agent, the text of the decision of patentability and its rationale, and number of claims to be patented, day/month/year of decision to grant a patent, matters having amended ex officio, along with an examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory checklist of items to appear in the grant decision (so the grant decision is a complete, signed, and dated document showing rationale and any ex-officio amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and confirmation of grant decision
rubrics_metrics.description: For a decision to grant a patent, the Commissioner of KIPO shall deliver a certified copy of the written decision to grant a patent to an applicant. The decision to grant a patent is confirmed upon the delivery of the certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act of delivery of the certified copy is the event that confirms the grant decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special review for applications filed by KIPO-related persons
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed by (1) a KIPO patent examiner, (2) a KIPO examiner within 2 years from retirement, and (3) a searcher of a prior art search institution supervised by KIPO, if the patent examiner finds registration is appropriate, the examiner shall determine grant or refusal in consultation with 3 persons including a director of the examination division or a head of the examination part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires consultation with additional senior staff to avoid conflict of interest and ensure independent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to make a written decision to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner provides an opportunity for petition with the notice of grounds for rejection, he/she shall make a decision to reject an application in writing with rationale attached if an applicant fails to overcome the grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground of rejection may be cured by ex-officio amendment, the examiner shall make the amendment and allow grant instead of issuing a rejection; see listed matters subject to ex-officio amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of written decision to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: The written decision to reject an application shall include an application number, title of invention, name and address of applicant and agent, day/month/year of notice of grounds for rejection, the text of decision and its rationale, and day/month/year of decision to reject a patent, along with an examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-to-reject documents must mirror the grant decision's required metadata and provide an explicit rationale; these are formalized requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and confirmation of rejection decision
rubrics_metrics.description: For decision to reject an application, the Commissioner of KIPO shall deliver a certified copy of the written decision to reject an application to an applicant. The decision to reject is confirmed when it cannot be revoked with methods prescribed in the Patent Act (e.g., no appeal filed in statutory period, appellate/trial decision supporting rejection, dismissal of trial request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery of certified copy plus elapse of remedies or adverse trial outcomes constitutes final confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner indication on applicant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: For decision to reject an application, an examiner shall indicate his or her determination on the applicant’s amendment in which the notified grounds for rejections were still not overcome and the issuable items in the written argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must state specifically which notified grounds remain and what issues are still open in the applicant's submitted amendment/argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection where any claim contains grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application involving two or more claims, where any of the claims contain grounds for rejection, an examiner shall make a decision to reject an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at least one claim is unallowable for notified grounds, the whole application is to be rejected (unless corrected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unreasonable grounds in rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall not make a decision to reject based on unreasonable rationale other than the already notified ground for rejection, which includes additional request for new documents relating to prior art. To refer a new prior art, an examiner shall notify the very fact as a ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must avoid surfacing new, unnotified reasons in a final rejection; newly found prior art requires explicit notification as a new ground rather than hidden introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty when third-party information used in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining an application with information provided by a third party as grounds for rejection, an examiner shall notify the information provider of his/her decision and whether the provided information is used or not in the examination when the examination closes, except where the provider lacked capacity or the application was abandoned, withdrawn, or invalidated prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At close of examination the third-party contributor must be informed whether their submission affected the outcome (with specified exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify legitimate right-holder for unentitled filer
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner decides to reject an application based on the ground that the application is filed by an unentitled person, he/she shall deliver written notice to the legitimate right-holder without delay after confirming the decision to reject. If confirmation will be long due because of appeal, examiner may notify the legitimate right-holder in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects rightful owners by prompt notice when an application by an unentitled filer is rejected; allows advance notice when confirmation delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation for revoked-and-returned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: As for the patent application which has been revoked and returned, the examiner responsible shall consult with a director of the examination division or a head of the examination part and determine allowance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires supervisory consultation when the procedural history includes revocation and return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of examination measures — grounds and retroactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner discovers defects in his/her measures during the examination, the very examiner may cancel the measures. The cancellation of a measure loses its partial or whole validity retroactively to the very beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation is available when prior measures display definite defects; cancellation acts retrospectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may cancel measures and balancing test
rubrics_metrics.description: Any cancellation shall be made under the name of the examiner who originally conducted the concerned measure. The measure can be cancelled only when the concerned measure displays definite defects and the benefits of its cancellation far outweigh the benefits of its maintaining — a comparative analysis between 'principle of law compliance' and 'principle of confidence protection'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancelling an examiner's action requires weighing legal compliance benefits against harm to reliance/confidence; high threshold for cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items generally not subject to cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: For notice of the ground for rejection, request for amendment, and request for supplementation, an examiner shall not cancel them because their cancellation is of less practical use compared to keeping them through amendment or error correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine procedural notices should generally remain in the record rather than be canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement on cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: A cancellation of a measure having been carried out by an examiner shall be notified to an applicant with definite and specific explanation of the measure to be cancelled and its corresponding reasons after communication to a managing director of the Examination Bureau following a head of the Examination Part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation must be communicated to applicant with specific reasons and after internal communications to management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and exceptional channel for cancellation notices
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, the cancellation shall be made in the form of a notice for cancellation provided by the Patent Examination Processing System. However, the On-nara System (EDMS) can be used in certain cases (three months past delivery due date, new documents received after delivering the notice of the measure, fee payment not completed, or failures in other systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard system form except defined exceptional circumstances where EDMS/On-nara may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to execute subsequent measures after self-cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: When cancelling the measure having been conducted by himself/herself, the concerned examiner shall execute the corresponding subsequent measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner who cancels own action must follow up with required next steps to maintain procedure integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days from the date of receiving a certified copy of the decision to reject a patent application (or within the extended period if extended), the applicant may amend the specification or drawing(s) to request reexamination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination window is tightly timed and is invoked by submitting an amendment within the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination is introduced to reduce the patent fee burden and complexity in the previous system of reexamination before an appeal trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rationale: an internal remedial stage to reduce cost/complexity versus formal appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination shall be assigned to the examiner who had performed the original examination and had decided to reject an application. However, if entrustment to the original examiner is not appropriate (e.g., transfer to non-exam bureau), an examiner in charge of patent classification of the claimed invention shall carry out the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer continuity (original examiner) unless inappropriate; use classification-expert if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for reexamination: an application has not been invalidated, withdrawn or abandoned; has been rejected (excluding rejection after reexamination); has not requested an appeal trial against decision to reject; and declares intention to request reexamination with amendment of the specification, drawing(s), or claims. 'Amendment' includes substantial and non-substantial changes to the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist to confirm a valid reexamination request; appeal pending or certain other statuses bar reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination of reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for reexamination shall be made by submission of the amendment. Therefore, the examination of formalities for reexamination request shall be made in accordance with the examination of amendment procedure. If defects (not pending, filed by non-applicant, submitted after statutory period), the examiner shall provide opportunity for explanation and return the written reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination requests are treated as amendments for formality review; defective requests are returned after opportunity to explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of reexamination where appeal trial requested
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall not request reexamination for an application for which an appeal trial against the decision to reject has been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutually exclusive remedies: appeals and reexamination cannot be pursued simultaneously by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling simultaneous appeal notice and amendment (case 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submits an amendment purporting reexamination after submitting a notice of appeal, the amendment must be returned — applicant may withdraw appeal and file reexamination request within prescribed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the appeal precedes the amendment, the amendment is invalid; applicant may opt to withdraw appeal to pursue reexamination if timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling simultaneous amendment then appeal (case 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submits a notice of appeal following submission of the amendment containing purport for reexamination, the amendment is legitimate and the examiner shall regard the decision to reject as cancelled and proceed with reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment-first sequence favors reexamination even if appeal notice follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling same-day submissions when order unclear (case 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submits notice of appeal and amendment on same day and submission times are not confirmed, examiner shall consider amendment submitted later than notice of appeal, notify reason for returning amendment, and explain that applicant may choose between reexamination and appeal. If applicant withdraws appeal, examiner will proceed with reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity resolved against amendment; examiner must give explanatory return notice and allow applicant choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling same-day amendment lacking reexamination purport (case 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submits a notice of appeal and an amendment without stating purport to request reexamination, both dated same day, the amendment not stating purport shall not be regarded as validly submitted within the amendment period and shall be treated as submitted after prescribed period; examiner shall return the amendment after giving opportunity for petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment must expressly state reexamination purport to be timely when filed same day as appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reexamination request on previous rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of reexamination request, the previous decision to reject is deemed to have been withdrawn. Examiner shall examine in same manner as before the rejection was made. However, prior procedures (notices, amendments, etc.) remain valid during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination vacates the prior final rejection but preserves prior procedural acts for continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-admission judgment to refuse entry of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendment is submitted to file reexamination request, an examiner, before conducting reexamination, shall confirm whether the amendment shall be refused to be entered or not. Judgment to refuse entry refers to the requirements in '11.2 Requirements for Amendment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must check amendment admissibility under amendment rules before full reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of amendment upon reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of amendment upon the request for reexamination is the same as that of amendment according to the final rejection necessitated by amendment; see Part VI Chapter 2 for scope rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment limits mirror those applicable when final rejection required amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for amendments submitted before reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the amendment that was conducted before the reexamination request is to be refused to be entered but is disregarded, an examiner shall not refuse to enter the aforesaid reason retroactively (Patent Act Article 51 proviso). This protects applicant's confidence and interest in reexamination procedure based on amendment made before decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are protected from retroactive rejection of amendments relied upon when requesting reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison rules for assessing new matter in successive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision as to whether the amendment is appropriately made is made by comparing added matter under Article 47(2) with the specification/drawings originally attached, and other Article 47(3) requirements compared to the specification/drawings having reflected prior amendments — context-dependent comparisons for sequences of Amendment I/II/III/IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple amendments and refusals occur, the comparator for 'new matter' may be original spec or a previously-admitted amendment depending on procedural history; follow the stepwise comparison rules given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission and effect of appropriate amendment in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment is regarded as appropriate, the examiner shall admit and reflect the amendment to the specification to be examined. After confirming the specification, he/she shall decide whether there are grounds for rejection or not, and make a decision to grant a patent or reject the application. In determining consequence, it may be decided in consultation with 3 persons including a patent examiner responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate amendments are entered into the record and reexamination proceeds to final determination; consultative decision allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying newly found grounds during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner considers the amendment overcomes the notified rejection grounds but discovers other rejection grounds that were not indicated, the examiner shall notify newly found grounds for rejection to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must give notice of newly discovered grounds rather than hide them in a final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retroactive refusal of entered amendments after issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner disregards a partial inappropriateness in the amendment upon the request for reexamination and issues a non-final rejection or a final rejection necessitated by amendment or the decision to grant a patent, the amendment shall not be refused to be entered retroactively even when the inappropriateness is discovered afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an amendment has been treated as entered and used to proceed to a rejection/grant, it will not later be retroactively un-entered for minor inappropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure after refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: After refusing to enter the amendment, an examiner shall immediately proceed with the pre-amendment original specification. If the grounds for rejection noticed are not amended, the examiner shall make a decision to reject. However, if review determines the decision to reject is not proper and discovers no other grounds, the examiner shall deliver a decision to grant a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to enter returns examination to the pre-amendment state; reviews can convert a rejection to allowance if no valid grounds remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination instruction on previously-notified grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the grounds for rejection having been notified previously are not overcome upon the reexamination request, those rejection grounds shall not be regarded newly generated. The examiner shall admit the amendment but make a decision to reject a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously-notified grounds that remain uncorrected after reexamination are treated as existing, not new, and justify rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on applicant actions during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When the request for reexamination is filed, the decision to reject a patent application is regarded as cancelled. Therefore, an applicant shall not perform acts which can be done within thirty days from receipt of a certified copy of the decision to reject (i.e., shall not file a notice of appeal or a divisional application), except an applicant may file a divisional either upon the request for a reexamination or within the period for submitting a written argument in response to the notice of grounds for rejection during the reexamination stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must not attempt to pursue simultaneous remedies that the law forbids during the reexamination period, with specific narrowly circumscribed exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal of reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 67-2(3) of the Patent Act stipulates that the request for a reexamination shall not be withdrawn. A submitted request to withdraw shall be regarded as an uncertain type of document; examiner shall provide an opportunity for explanation and return the written request for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination requests are irrevocable; withdrawal documents are treated as defective and returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple amendments same-day rule for reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment stating the purport for the reexamination request dated on the same day is submitted multiple times, any amendment from the second submission shall not be deemed to be submitted within the prescribed period. Subsequent amendments are regarded as submitted after statutory period and returned after opportunity for explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the first amendment on that day is treated as timely for reexamination purpose; duplicates are late.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination standard for amendments on reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: In examining the application to which an amendment is made upon request for reexamination, it shall be determined whether a ground of rejection, which has been notified through a decision to reject, is remedied by amendment. Even if the amendment fails to remedy other grounds, examiner shall provide opportunity for written arguments without issuing a decision to reject; however, if the amended application includes a ground of rejection once overcome by previous amendment to non-final rejection, a decision to reject shall be made because applicant had prior opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should allow written argument for newly uncovered grounds during reexamination except where applicant already had a chance to correct that ground previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-language application — permitted languages and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent applicant states intention to write the specification and drawings in a language specified by Ordinance (English), other than Korean, he/she may do so. Foreign-language specification is permitted only for establishing a filing date; Korean translations must be filed within prescribed periods because examination and rights are based on Korean specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-language filings are allowed to secure filing date but substantive prosecution and issuance rely on Korean translations filed timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korean translation submission time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant who submitted a foreign-language specification shall submit a Korean translation of the specification and drawings by not later than 1 year and 2 months from the date specified in Article 64(1). If a request for examination is received, the applicant shall submit Korean translation by not later than 3 months from the date when notice is served or 1 year 2 months from earliest priority date, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict deadlines apply; examiner must ensure translations are received before substantive acts (examination request, early publication, divisional, etc.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement Korean translations and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant who has submitted a Korean translation may submit another Korean translation in replacement by not later than the expiration of the translation period, except where the applicant has amended the specification or filed a request for examination. After request for examination or an amendment, new translations are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacements allowed only within initial translation window and pre-examination/amendment; prevents changing the Korean spec mid-prosecution to circumvent amendment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to submit Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant fails to submit a Korean translation of the specification under paragraph (2), the applicant shall be deemed to voluntarily withdraw the patent application on the next day after the expiration of the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely translate leads to automatic deemed withdrawal — fatal procedural consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing drawing translations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Korean translations of drawings (text matter only) are not submitted, the patent application shall not be deemed to have been withdrawn as is different from the case of a specification. However, amendment to the application may be instructed on grounds of violation of the written description requirement of drawing(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing drawing translations do not automatically withdraw the application but may trigger correction/amendment requirements related to written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of submitting Korean translations — deemed amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If Korean translations are submitted, the foreign-language specification originally attached shall be deemed amended according to the Korean translations. Translations shall be word-for-word in accordance with the context. New matter beyond original disclosure is evaluated based on Korean translations; mistranslations may be corrected within allowed amendment periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean translation becomes the operative text for scope and examination; accuracy and timing are critical — changes in translation can alter scope and may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational consequences after Korean translation submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Only after Korean translations being submitted can the applicant file a request for examination, amend the specification, file a divisional or converted application, and request early publication. Patent is granted after reviewing Korean specification and public inspection is in Korean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations gate access to procedural milestones and public rights establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on examining new matter in foreign-language applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination for a foreign patent application is basically the same as for regular applications. However, either amendment to a specification or amendment based on the Korean translation has its limits resulting from characteristics of foreign-language application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must apply standard examination rules but be mindful of additional constraints (e.g., on introducing new matter via translation) specific to foreign-language cases.
